label: START G1: long-acting bronchodilator in symptomatic COPD
title: Long-acting bronchodilator missing in symptomatic GOLD 1 or 2 COPD
statement: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA e.g., tiotropium, aclidinium, umeclidinium, glycopyrronium) or long-acting beta 2 agonist (LABA e.g., bambuterol, formoterol, indacaterol, olodaterol, salmeterol) for symptomatic COPD of GOLD 1 or 2 severity and chronic asthma.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: A person with symptomatic COPD of mild or moderate severity (GOLD 1 or 2), or with chronic asthma, should usually have a long-acting inhaler to keep the airways open, and the record shows none. In Australia this criterion is applied to COPD only. Asthma is treated with an inhaled corticosteroid, and a long-acting beta agonist is never used without one (Australian Asthma Handbook).

medicine_groups.name: Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA) and long-acting beta 2 agonists (LABA), alone or in a combination inhaler

umeclidinium: Trelegy Ellipta (fluticasone furoate with umeclidinium and vilanterol)
vilanterol: Trelegy Ellipta (fluticasone furoate with umeclidinium and vilanterol)

medicine_groups.note: Medicines that meet this criterion. Bambuterol tablets are not sold in Australia, so no brand is listed. Inhaled steroid and long-acting beta 2 agonist combinations count because they contain a LABA. Eformoterol is another name for formoterol. Count it once. Count inhaled glycopyrronium for bronchodilation. Exclude glycopyrronium injection and oral solution. Oral bambuterol is named in the source.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that may suggest COPD
medicine_groups.note: Used to suspect the condition when no condition line exists. A reliever alone does not prove the condition. Exclude nasal ipratropium, including Atrovent Nasal, from the airway clues.

needs_facts.what: Symptomatic COPD with GOLD 1 or 2 airflow limitation
needs_facts.meets: The Australian screen requires documented COPD, symptoms attributable to COPD and GOLD 1 or 2 airflow limitation. Asthma alone does not qualify. If COPD is recorded and symptoms or stage are unknown, report at most a possible finding. No COPD finding applies to documented absence of symptoms or GOLD 3 or 4.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion from age 65 and give no finding below 65, for asthma alone, for documented absence of COPD symptoms, for GOLD 3 or 4, or if any Group A LAMA or LABA was supplied in the last six months (oral bambuterol counts, and glycopyrronium counts only when inhaled for bronchodilation). At a confirmed age of 65 or older, suspect an omission if no Group A medicine was supplied in those six months and cite the lines showing COPD, symptoms attributable to COPD and GOLD 1 or 2 airflow limitation. If COPD is recorded or a Group B supply other than nasal ipratropium suggests it, report only a possible finding when facts are missing and name what needs confirmation: age, COPD diagnosis, symptoms or GOLD stage.
cannot_be_seen: The record may omit COPD symptoms, the GOLD stage, a reason a long-acting inhaler was stopped, supplies from a hospital or another pharmacy, and whether the person is near the end of life.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether a long-acting inhaler is needed, with a check of the diagnosis and its stage.
